sentences.text: 1. Being dissatisfied with the award of compensation of Rs.2,15,091/-, the claimant is in this appeal seeking enhancement.
2. The occurrence of the accident and the liability to pay compensation by the Insurer are not in dispute.
3. The appellant - claimant has suffered a fracture of right angle of the mandible and blunt injury to chest and abdomen.

The doctor who was examined as P.W.4 has stated that as a result of the accident, the appellant was unable to chew food and was unable to approximate upper and lower jaw teeth, as a result of which he has lost weight.
He has ultimately stated that claimant has suffered 21% disability.
The Tribunal, on consideration of this evidence, has come to the conclusion that the claimant was disabled to the extent of 7% to the whole body.
In my view, due to malalignment of upper and lower jaw, the claimant has difficulty in chewing the food, and therefore, it would be appropriate to treat the whole body disability at 10%.
5. The Tribunal has taken the notional income of the claimant as Rs.8,000/-, since there was no evidence to that effect.

As the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority has determined the notional income as Rs.9,500/- for the accident of the year 2016, it would be appropriate to determine the notional income of the claimant at Rs.9,500/-.
6. Since the claimant was aged 41 years, the appropriate multiplier would be '14'.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,59,600/- (Rs.9,500/- X 12 X '14' X 10%) towards 'loss of future earnings'.

7. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/-
towards 'pain and suffering and Rs.25,000/- towards NC: 2024:KHC:45991 'loss of amenities,
conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges'.

In my view, since the claimant has suffered fracture of right mandible and has sustained blunt injury to chest and abdomen, it would be appropriate to enhance the compensation to Rs.50,000/- under the heads 'pain and suffering' and 'loss of amenities'.
8. A sum of Rs.18,251/- awarded towards medical bills is just and proper and is affirmed.
9. The Tribunal has treated the laid-up period as four months.

Since the monthly income is now enhanced to Rs.9,500/-, the claimant is entitled to a sum of Rs.38,000/-.
10.
The claimant was hospitalized for 38 days.
In my view, it would be appropriate to award Rs.40,000/- towards 'conveyance, food and attendant charges'.

12 . Accordingly, the claimant is held entitled to a compensation of Rs.3,55,851/- as against Rs.2,15,091/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the enhanced compensation amount from the date of petition till its realisation.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
14. The other aspects of the Award of the Tribunal remain undisturbed.
15. This appeal is, accordingly, allowed in part.
